prompt:
[quiet, tired] A ring of coarse salt, a finger thick. Broken and poured again in two places — where he crawled out for water.

The cooler is a third empty. One pack of crackers left, the last. Six nights on this.

[quiet, reading] Sheets taped to the rack. One handwriting, different nights: 'Don't call me.' 'Knock three times.' 'It speaks in my mother's voice.'

[quiet, careful] Was it really… her?

[quiet, tired] Gus said he gets called too. Martha.

Why salt?

I'll sit with you till six.

[hoarse, tired, firm] The voice is hers. Down to the last note, the way she called me to dinner. But my mother died in ninety-six, son. It's not her.

[hoarse, tired] I know. Thirty years he's been going up to seven to listen to her. It doesn't touch him — he never answers. He just listens. That's a way to live, too.

I don't know why. I know it works. My father did it, his father did it. As long as the ring holds, it can only talk.

[hoarse, quiet] Sit. But if they call — not a word. Even in my voice.
